failure_modes.name: Missing_Evidence_Not_Specified
failure_modes.evidence: Summary 1: 'there is no information in the passages about an MTV show called "You Can't See Me" or about any member of the Likwit Crew hosting such a show.' Summary 2: 'The passages do not contain any information about an MTV show titled "You Can't See Me," nor do they provide evidence of any connection between Defari, the Likwit Crew, or any band member to such a show.' Neither summary names the specific missing entity needed: which member of Likwit Crew allegedly hosted the show, or what "You Can't See Me" actually is as an MTV program.

failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Query 1: 'MTV show "You Can't See Me" host Likwit Crew member' is a compound multi-part query bundling three targets (the show, its host, and band membership) into unstructured keyword soup. Query 3: 'You Can't See Me MTV show' remains keyword-based without clear target structure.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Query 1: 'MTV show "You Can't See Me" host Likwit Crew member' and Query 3: 'You Can't See Me MTV show' both chase the same entity (the show "You Can't See Me") with near-identical terms, failing to advance after summaries 1 and 2 both indicated this approach yielded no relevant information.

failure_modes.name: Insufficient_Retrieved_Evidence
failure_modes.evidence: Summary 2 names the missing entity: 'an MTV show titled "You Can't See Me"' and Query 3 targets it: 'You Can't See Me MTV show'. However, all three retrieval hops failed to retrieve any passage about an MTV show with this title; the closest retrieved was 'You Can't See 'round Corners' (a 1969 film/TV show, not MTV) and various songs with similar titles. This represents a corpus coverage gap.

failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: Solver 1 reasoning discusses passage [6] 'I Can't See Me Without You' by Conway Twitty: 'Looking through the passages, I can find information about MTV shows... Passage [7] mentions Heather B. was on "The Real World"' — analyzing clearly irrelevant country music and unrelated MTV shows rather than focusing on the core evidence gap about Likwit Crew members hosting MTV shows.
